summary: A 60-foot steel fire lookout on American Camp Peak in Tuolumne County, built in 1930 by state foresters, operated until 1969, and now a standing ruin.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot steel observation cab

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Stanislaus National Forest (Mi-Wok Ranger District)

Plan announced to replace the tree platform with a 50-foot steel tower
60-foot steel tower built by state foresters with a 7-by-7-foot cab
Newspaper reports J.H. Kling had served three years as American Camp lookout

corrections.why: The register and the Stanislaus album both give the built tower as 60 ft (about 18.3 m). The 15.2 m figure matches the 50-foot tower announced in a 1929 newspaper item, which was not the tower built.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1929 item planned a 50-foot tower, but a 1930 item describes a 60-foot tower under construction. The register and the Stanislaus album both give 60 feet for the standing tower.

notes_for_editor: Correction proposed for height_m (15.2 to 18.3). Access and visiting status were not found in any source, so no access key is set. The Stanislaus album dated 2022 is the most recent source. The 1932 Kling item is the only staffing name found. No notable fires found.
